hero_title: We raise talent. The Global Goals get the dividend.
hero_lead: AfriCloud Institute is an NGO. Scholarships, mentors, and community are how we contribute to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals: quality education, decent work, innovation, equality, and partnership.

mission.title: Our Mission
mission.text: Award full scholarships. Mentor African talent in technology. Send them into the world job-ready, and send some of them out as founders who give back at home.

vision.title: Our Vision
vision.text: An Africa where hunger beats hardship: drive, not tuition, decides who enters tech, and talent stays long enough to raise the next table.

agenda_note: Our work is framed by the UN 2030 Agenda and supports the African Union’s Agenda 2063: a prosperous Africa based on inclusive growth, and a continent whose youth are skilled, employed, and entrepreneurial.

core_values.title: Excellence
core_values.text: We hold a high bar for skills, teaching quality, and the work scholars produce. Job-ready means the work would stand up on a real team.

core_values.title: Equity
core_values.text: A full scholarship is the point. Talent from across Africa, including young women and people locked out by cost, should be able to start.

core_values.title: Community
core_values.text: We raise people together. Mentorship, peer support, and scholar communities last beyond class and fold back into African neighbourhoods and teams.

core_values.title: Innovation
core_values.text: Curriculum stays with current tools and ways of working: cloud, DevOps, AI, cybersecurity, data, and software used in industry today.

core_values.title: Integrity
core_values.text: Scholarships are free. Nobody should pay for a seat or a certificate. We are transparent about programmes and how we handle scholar data.

core_values.title: Partnership
core_values.text: SDG 17 is how scale happens. We work with organisations that sponsor scholars, host internships, send mentors, and open doors to work.

goals.title: Our Goals
goals.intro: What we organise the NGO around. Each one maps to the dashboard below.

entries.title: Remove tuition as a barrier
entries.text: Award full scholarships so African talent can enter Cloud, DevOps, AI, Cybersecurity, data, and software without paying course fees.

entries.title: Make scholars job-ready
entries.text: Deliver live mentoring, labs, and portfolios that match what teams hire for, not theory alone.

entries.title: Raise entrepreneurs
entries.text: Mentor builders who will launch and grow African ventures, not only fill roles.

entries.title: Widen who gets in
entries.text: Prioritise inclusion: young people, career changers, women in tech, and learners from communities that rarely see this pathway.

entries.title: Turn skills into work
entries.text: Grow a partner network that offers internships, apprenticeships, project briefs, and first roles.

entries.title: Stay accountable
entries.text: Publish how our programmes contribute to the SDGs, and keep selection, classrooms, and data handling honest.

initiatives.title: Our Initiatives
initiatives.intro: Five doors. One promise: African talent should not stall at the fee page.

entries.title: AfriCloud Scholars
entries.text: Full scholarships for live, remote bootcamps. Every seat is funded. Scholars choose a pathway and join a cohort: no tuition, no hidden course fee.

entries.title: MentorCircle
entries.text: Instructor-led teaching plus mentors who stay close. The scholar WhatsApp community carries class, peer support, and accountability between sessions.

entries.title: JobReady Studio
entries.text: Hands-on labs, portfolio projects, and career coaching so graduates can interview, contribute, and stay employed.

entries.title: Venture Lab
entries.text: Mentorship for scholars who will found and grow. Problem-solving, product thinking, and the discipline to ship, so Africa’s next ventures have operators, not only ideas.

entries.title: Partner Alliance
entries.text: Companies, NGOs, and community hosts sponsor scholars, offer internships, send mentors, or run a local circle with us.

dashboard.title: Our SDG Action Dashboard
dashboard.intro: We do not pretend to deliver all 17 Goals. We go deep where scholarships and mentors actually move the needle.
dashboard.footnote: Target language follows the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. Our contribution is through education, mentoring, employment pathways, entrepreneurship, inclusion, and partnership, not through unaudited impact claims.

sdgs.name: Quality Education

targets.text: Equal access to affordable, quality technical, vocational, and tertiary education.
Increase the number of youth and adults with relevant skills, including technical and vocational skills, for employment, decent jobs, and entrepreneurship.

sdgs.action: AfriCloud Scholars and MentorCircle award full scholarships and live vocational training in Cloud, DevOps, AI, Cybersecurity, data, and software. JobReady Studio and Venture Lab are how Target 4.4 shows up in practice: skills for jobs and for founding.

sdgs.name: Gender Equality

targets.text: Ensure women’s full and effective participation and equal opportunities in economic life.
Enhance the use of enabling technology to promote the empowerment of women.

sdgs.action: Tech careers and founder pathways must be open to young women, not reserved for those who can pay. We recruit and mentor women into the same fully funded cohorts, and we ask partners to keep internships and apprenticeships equally accessible.

sdgs.name: Decent Work and Economic Growth

targets.text: Promote development-oriented policies that support decent job creation, entrepreneurship, creativity, and innovation.
Reduce the proportion of youth not in employment, education, or training.

sdgs.action: JobReady Studio prepares scholars for decent work. Venture Lab prepares them to create work. Partner Alliance connects cohorts to internships and first roles so training does not end at a certificate.

sdgs.name: Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure

targets.text: Support domestic technology development, research, and innovation.
Significantly increase access to information and communications technology.

sdgs.action: Remote, Africa-first cohorts widen access to ICT skills. Venture Lab and advanced tracks (cloud, AI, security, software) build the people African industry needs to innovate, not only consume technology.

sdgs.name: Reduced Inequalities

targets.text: Empower and promote the social and economic inclusion of all, irrespective of origin or other status.

sdgs.action: Tuition is one of the sharpest filters in tech. Full scholarships, remote delivery, and community mentoring are how we include African talent who would otherwise be locked out of global-standard training.

sdgs.name: Partnerships for the Goals

targets.text: Encourage and promote effective public, public-private, and civil society partnerships.

sdgs.action: Partner Alliance is our SDG 17 mechanism: organisations sponsor seats, host internships, send mentors, and help communities run local circles. The NGO cannot raise a generation of talent alone.

steps.title: Access
steps.text: A full scholarship takes the price off the table.

steps.title: Skills
steps.text: Live mentors and labs make the work real.

steps.title: Work & ventures
steps.text: Career coaching and founder support turn skill into income and into companies.

steps.title: Community
steps.text: Scholars stay. They hold the door. The next cohort is easier to raise.

invite.title: Come as a scholar. Stay as a builder. Return as a mentor.
invite.text: This NGO is a relay. You run your leg. Then you pass the baton.
